Everyday I usually have 1 cup (2 servings) of instant white rice. It's easy to microwave at my office and I get a decent amount of carbs, the macro I have the most trouble taking in enough of. Honestly, its not clear what you are asking... brown rice is generally regarded as clearly healthier, but what nutrients are you worried about missing out on?

IMO, the biggest advantage of brown rice over white is the glycemic index (see here). That said, glycemic index is mostly something you worry about when you are trying to cut or lose weight.

Other than the glycemic index, I don't think there is a substantial difference between white and brown rice, I mean, brown has a bit more of a slew of micro nutrients, but if you are eating veggies/fruit in moderate quantities, you shouldn't need to get those from your rice.

In summary, yes, brown is a bit better, but if its an inconvenience, I would say not worth the benefits.

Combine 1 cup brown rice, 3 cups water in a 2 ½ quart microwave-safe dish. Microwave UNCOVERED on HIGH for 10 minutes. REDUCE power to 50%, microwave uncovered 20 minutes. Allow rice to sit for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and serve. Do not add salt or butter/margarine to the rice until AFTER the rice is cooked.
Brown rice has more fiber which you may not want in a bulk. White rice is more easily absorbed.

Growing up, I always called the act of writing code 'programming'. In recent years the word 'coding' has become much more popular. I myself have been calling it coding lately just because I hear it so much, however, it does seem like a pretentious word.

Coding: writing code in an unplanned/intuitive way (i.e. more freelance)
